sentences.en: HAZEL: Tom, could I ask you for some advice, please?
sentences.zh: HAZEL: Tom，我能向你请教一些建议吗？

sentences.en: TOM: Yes of course, if you think I can help.
sentences.zh: TOM: 当然可以，如果你觉得我能帮上忙的话。

sentences.en: What's it about?
sentences.zh: 这是关于什么的？

sentences.en: HAZEL: It's my first media studies assignment, and I'm not sure how to go about it.
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 这是我第一次做媒体研究课程的作业，我不太确定该从何入手。

sentences.en: You must have done it last year.
sentences.zh: 你去年肯定做过这个作业。

sentences.en: TOM: Is that the one comparing the coverage of a particular story in a range of newspapers?
sentences.zh: TOM: 是那个比较同一则新闻故事在多家报纸中报道方式的作业吗？

sentences.en: HAZEL: That's right.
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 没错。

sentences.en: TOM: Oh yes, really enjoyed writing it.
sentences.zh: TOM: 哦，是的，写起来真的很有趣。

sentences.en: HAZEL: So what sort of things do l need to compare?
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 那么我需要比较哪些方面呢？

sentences.en: TOM: Well, there are several things.
sentences.zh: TOM: 嗯，需要比较的方面有好几个。

sentences.en: For example, there's the question of which page of the newspaper the item appears on.
sentences.zh: 例如，这篇报道刊登在报纸的哪一版上。

sentences.en: Audioscripts HAZEL You mean, because there's a big difference between having it on the front page and the bottom of page ten, for instance?
sentences.zh: 听力原文 HAZEL：你的意思是，比如登在头版和登在第十页底部，这两者之间存在很大差别，对吗？

sentences.en: TOM: Exactly.
sentences.zh: TOM: 没错。

sentences.en: And that shows how important the editor thinks the story is.
sentences.zh: 这反映出编辑认为该新闻的重要性如何。

sentences.en: Then there's the size - how many column inches the story is given, how many columns it spreads over.
sentences.zh: 然后是篇幅——报道所占的栏英寸数、横跨几栏。

sentences.en: HAZEL: And suppose that includes the headline.
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 假设这包括了标题部分。

sentences.en: TOM: It certainly does.
sentences.zh: TOM: 当然包括。

sentences.en: It's all part of attracting the reader's attention.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都旨在吸引读者的注意力。

sentences.en: HAZEL: What about graphics - whether there's anything visual in addition to the text?
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 那么配图呢——即除了文字之外是否还有其他视觉元素？

sentences.en: TOM: Yes, you need to consider those, too, because they can have a big effect on the reader's understanding of the story - sometimes a bigger effect than the text itself.
sentences.zh: TOM: 对，这些你也需要考虑，因为它们会对读者理解新闻产生很大影响——有时甚至比文字本身的影响还要大。

sentences.en: Then you'll need to look at how the item is put together: what structure is it given?
sentences.zh: 然后，你需要观察这个物品是如何组合起来的：它采用了什么样的结构？

sentences.en: Bear in mind that not many people read beyond the first paragraph, SO what has the journalist put at the beginning?
sentences.zh: 请记住，很少有人会读完第一段，那么记者把什么放在了开头？

sentences.en: And if, say, there are conflicting opinions about something, does one appear near the end, where people probably won't read it?
sentences.zh: 而且，如果比如说，对某件事存在相互冲突的观点，其中一个观点是否出现在末尾，而人们很可能不会读到那里？

sentences.en: HAZEL: And newspapers sometimes give wrong or misleading information, don't they?
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 而且报纸有时会提供错误或具有误导性的信息，不是吗？

sentences.en: Either deliberately or by accident.
sentences.zh: 要么是故意的，要么是无意的。

sentences.en: Should I be looking at that, too?
sentences.zh: 我也应该关注这一点吗？

sentences.en: TOM: Yes, if you can.
sentences.zh: TOM: 是的，如果可以的话。

sentences.en: Compare what's in different versions, and as far as possible, try and work out what's true and what isn't.
sentences.zh: 比较不同版本中的内容，并尽可能弄清楚哪些是真实的、哪些不是。

sentences.en: And that relates to a very important
sentences.zh: 而这关联到一个非常重要的

sentences.en: point: what's the writer's purpose, or at least the most important one, if they have several.
sentences.zh: 要点：作者的写作目的，或者至少是其最主要的目的（如果作者有多个目的的话）。

sentences.en: It may seem to be to inform the public, but often it's that they want to create fear, or controversy, or to make somebody look ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 表面看来，其目的似乎是向公众传递信息，但往往真实意图是制造恐惧、引发争议，或让某人显得荒谬可笑。

sentences.en: HAZEL: Gosh, I see what you mean.
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 哎呀，我明白你的意思了。

sentences.en: And I suppose the writer may make assumptions about the reader.
sentences.zh: 我想作者可能还会对读者做出某些假设。

sentences.en: TOM: That's right - about their knowledge of the subject, their attitudes, and their level of education, which means writing so that the readers understand without feeling patronised.
sentences.zh: TOM: 没错——比如假设读者对该主题的了解程度、他们的态度以及受教育水平，这意味着作者需以一种既能让读者理解、又不会让他们感到被居高临下对待的方式进行写作。

sentences.en: All of that will make a difference to how the story is presented.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素都会影响新闻故事的呈现方式。

sentences.en: HAZEL: Does it matter what type of story I write about?
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 我所写的新闻类型重要吗？

sentences.en: TOM: No - national or international politics, the arts ...
sentences.zh: TOM: 不重要——无论是国内还是国际政治、艺术领域……

sentences.en: Anything, as long as it's covered in two or three newspapers.
sentences.zh: 任何题材都可以，只要它在两到三家报纸中都有报道。

sentences.en: Though of course it'll be easier and more fun if it's something you're interested in and know something about.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你选择自己感兴趣且有一定了解的话题，分析起来会更容易、也更有趣。

sentences.en: HAZEL: And on that basis a national news item would be worth analysing - I'm quite keen on politics, so I'll try and find a suitable topic.
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 基于此，一篇国内新闻事件就值得分析——我对政治相当感兴趣，因此我会努力找一个合适的话题。

sentences.en: What did you choose for your analysis, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你选择什么作为你的分析对象，汤姆？

sentences.en: TOM: I was interested in how newspapers express their opinions explicitly, sO I wanted to compare editorials in different papers, but when I started looking, L couldn't find two on the same topic that I felt like analysing.
sentences.zh: TOM: 我对报纸如何明确表达其观点很感兴趣，因此我想比较不同报纸的社论，但当我开始查找时，却找不到两篇关于同一主题、且我觉得适合分析的社论。

sentences.en: HAZEL: In that case, I won't even bother to look.
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 那样的话，我干脆连找都懒得找了。

sentences.en: TOM: So in the end I chose a human a interest story - a terribly emotional story about a young girl who was very ill, and lots of other people mostly strangers - raised money so she could go abroad for treatment.
sentences.zh: TOM: 所以最后我选了一则人文类新闻故事——一则令人极度动容的故事，讲述一名身患重病的年轻女孩，以及许多素不相识的人如何为她筹款，使她得以赴海外接受治疗。

sentences.en: Actually, was surprised - some papers just wrote about how wonderful everyone was, but others considered the broader picture, like why treatment wasn't available here.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我感到很惊讶——有些报纸只是单纯报道大家多么了不起，而另一些报纸则着眼于更宏观的层面，比如探讨为何此类治疗在国内无法获得。

sentences.en: HAZEL: Hmm, I usually find stories like that raise quite strong feelings in me!
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 嗯，这类故事通常会在我心中激起相当强烈的情感！

sentences.en: I'lL avoid that.
sentences.zh: 我得避开这类题材。

sentences.en: Perhaps I'll choose an arts topic, like different reviews of a film, or something about funding for the arts I'll think about that.
sentences.zh: 也许我会选择一个艺术类话题，比如针对同一部电影的不同影评，或者有关艺术资助的相关报道；我会再考虑一下。

sentences.en: TOM: Yes, that might be interesting.
sentences.zh: TOM: 是的，这或许会很有意思。

sentences.en: HAZEL: OK, well thanks a lot for your help, Tom.
sentences.zh: HAZEL: 好的，非常感谢你的帮助，汤姆。

sentences.en: It's been really useful.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: TOM: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: TOM: 不客气。

sentences.en: Good luck with the assignment, Hazel.
sentences.zh: 祝你作业顺利，海泽尔。
